app.title: Polyglot Assist
app.no_answer_hint: Is the integration loaded? Settings → Devices & services → Polyglot Assist.

tips.how: Polyglot listens first to every voice command. If it knows the sentence, it carries it out right away, without AI and in the language you spoke. Otherwise it passes it on to your AI assistant.
tips.proposals: This is where Polyglot collects new, changed and to-be-removed commands, sentences and names. None of it is active until you accept it. Every suggestion has been checked: it must not interfere with any other command, and everything that already works must keep working.
tips.starter: The AI looks at your scripts, scenes and devices that Polyglot doesn't understand yet and suggests commands and names in all selected languages, plus types for your commands. Ideal for the first setup.
tips.newdev: After adding a new integration or device: Polyglot finds what's new and suggests names and commands.
tips.coverage: How many example sentences there are per language. Orange: one language has noticeably fewer variants than the others. With “Translate” the AI suggests the missing ones.
tips.safety: Normal: the command runs right away. Security-related (e.g. front door, garage, car): it runs, but is marked; Polyglot never accepts suggestions for it automatically, and you get a warning when changing it. Off: Polyglot ignores the command and the sentence goes to your AI assistant.
tips.groups: Type: lights, energy, weather … (can be set for each command). Polyglot works out the room and device from the devices a command controls.
tips.cats: Types organize your commands. You can add your own, rename them or delete them. When you delete a type, its commands move to “Other”.
tips.syntax: [square brackets] = optional · (a|b) = one of them · {placeholder} = a room, device or number that Polyglot fills in.
tips.answer: Speak: “Couch light on.” Sound: a short chime (needs Polyglot TTS). Only applies to control commands; questions are always answered out loud.
tips.kind: Control command: does something (light on …). Question: gives you information (weather, status …) and is always answered out loud.
tips.test: Type a sentence the way you would say it. Polyglot shows whether and how it understands it. Nothing gets switched.
tips.corpus: Real sentences from your everyday life that must always be understood the same way. Polyglot checks them before every change; if something would break, nothing is saved.
tips.names: What you call rooms and devices in each language, e.g. living room = Wohnzimmer = salon. These names don't change anything in Home Assistant itself and don't slow down your AI assistant.
tips.monitor: Polyglot remembers the last 500 voice commands (text only, no audio, stays in your Home Assistant). Once a day your own AI looks at what often wasn't understood directly and turns it into suggestions.
tips.languages: The languages spoken in your home. Polyglot detects them automatically; languages you deselect are no longer considered.
tips.aitask: The AI task that suggests translations, names and commands. It must not have any tools: it reads sentences from elsewhere and must not be able to control anything while doing so.
tips.builtin: Home Assistant comes with ready-made voice commands: lights on/off, dimming, color, timers, date, time, status. On its own, though, it only understands them in the language of your voice assistant. With this switch, Polyglot recognizes them in all selected languages and carries them out right away, without going through the AI. That's faster and also works when the AI can't be reached. Polyglot never controls doors, locks, gates, alarms or the car this way; such commands still go to your AI assistant. Only turn this off if you want to define all commands yourself.
tips.followup: So that your AI assistant understands “and now the piano too”, it is told what Polyglot just switched.
tips.fallback: Everything that is not a fixed command is answered by your AI assistant. Choose which one here. It cannot be Polyglot itself – the sentence would go round in circles forever.
tips.pipelines: A voice assistant in Home Assistant decides who listens (speech recognition), who understands (Polyglot should be here) and who speaks. “Prefer handling commands locally”: when on, Home Assistant checks every sentence itself first – only in the assistant's language – and Polyglot never sees those sentences. Off is right when Polyglot handles the built-in commands.
tips.apply: Polyglot will then only listen to the selected languages and load Home Assistant's built-in commands for them. This takes about a second. Your own commands stay as they are. At least one language must be selected.
tips.amp: For a sentence to work in a language, four things are needed: speech recognition must understand it, your AI must speak it, Polyglot must know commands in it, and speech output must be able to answer in it. Home Assistant does not report whether speech recognition detects the language by itself – “Test speech recognition” checks that.
tips.uitexts: The texts of this interface. German, English and French are included. For any other language your AI translates the texts; you can change every line. “Export” creates a file you can share with everyone.
tips.dry_run: Shows what the starter set would suggest – without putting anything into the suggestions and without remembering devices. Good for trying out an AI.
tips.tone: Home Assistant plays its own confirmation tone only for its built-in assistant. So that the tone works with any speech output, Polyglot brings a small speech output “Polyglot Assist (tone)”: it passes every text on to the speech output chosen here and only plays a short tone for switching commands. With Polyglot TTS you do not need this.
tips.voicelearn: You can talk about suggestions: “What have you learned?”, “Tell me more about the first one”, “Accept it” – Polyglot asks back and only applies it after your “Yes”. By voice, only new sentences and names for harmless commands are possible; anything security-related, new commands and protection levels stay in the panel. At most 5 per hour, only on the chosen devices, and “Undo that” takes it back within 24 hours.
tips.tonedesign: How a successful command is confirmed. Classic is the tone used so far. Design: notes, direction, style, pitch, sound. Or your own tone from a file or a recording.
tips.monreview: Language-independent: the AI reads conversations where you spoke again shortly after an action and recognises corrections such as “That's wrong, the bed light went off too”. Suggestions from them are always marked and can only be accepted in the panel – never by voice.
tips.answered: What is said when the command is recognised – per language, from text and current values. If the answer still comes from a YAML file, Polyglot takes it over for editing.

aed.title: Answer
aed.blocks_lost: Going back to blocks means starting over (“Start over with blocks”) – this template does not fit into blocks.
aed.draft_hint: The AI only changed the text; the values stayed the same. Please check, then save.
aed.empty: No answer in this language yet. Add a sentence or have it translated from another language.
aed.leave_warning: Unsaved answers – save or discard. Click again to leave (they are kept until you open another command).
aed.no_ai: First choose an AI task without tools under Settings.
aed.owned_hint: The YAML file stays unchanged but is no longer used for this command.
aed.pick_cond: What does the answer depend on?
aed.preview_note: with the current values · nothing is executed
aed.released: The YAML file answers again. Polyglot's version is in the history.
aed.release_text: From now on the YAML file answers again. Polyglot's answer is removed (restorable from the history).
aed.saved: Saved · test run {cases} sentences · can be undone in the history.
aed.shared_hint: One template for all languages (taken over from the YAML file; it handles the languages itself). Edit it here or start over per language with blocks.
aed.taken_over: Taken over – Polyglot answers from now on.
aed.takeover_q: Take the answer over into Polyglot?
aed.takeover_text: From now on Polyglot answers this command – with the answer and action from the YAML file. The file stays unchanged but is no longer used for this command. You can go back at any time.
aed.template_hint: Expert view (Jinja). Values and text as you like – what is here is spoken.
aed.tip: Tip: typing @ in a sentence inserts a value at the cursor. A value behaves like one character; click it to change it.
aed.yaml_card: Card and reprompt from the YAML file are not taken over.
aed.yaml_changed: The YAML file changed since it was taken over.
aed.yaml_hint: You can see and test it here. To edit it, Polyglot takes it over (answer and, if any, action).
aed.yaml_title: This answer lives in a YAML file (intent_script).
aed.yaml_vars: It uses values Polyglot does not know: {vars}.
aed.convert_failed: Converting to a template did not work just now – the blocks stay unchanged. Please try again.
